sentences.zh: （毛惜惜附）〉

translations.literal: (Mao Xixi appended)
translations.idiomatic: (with Mao Xixi appended)

sentences.zh: 古者天子親耕，教男子力作，皇后親蠶，教女子治生。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven personally plowed the fields, teaching men to labor with strength; the empress personally raised silkworms, teaching women to manage household production.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times the emperor himself plowed the fields to teach men the value of hard work, while the empress personally tended silkworms to teach women how to manage the household economy.

sentences.zh: 王道之本，風俗之原，固有在矣。

translations.literal: The foundation of kingly governance and the source of custom and mores have always lain in this.
translations.idiomatic: The foundations of righteous rule and the roots of social custom have always rested on such teachings.

sentences.zh: 男有塾師，女有師氏，國有其官，家有其訓，然而詩書所稱男女之賢，尚可數也。

translations.literal: Men had tutors in the village schools, women had instructresses; the state had its officials, families had their precepts—yet the worthy men and women praised in the Poetry and Documents can still be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Men had schoolmasters and women had instructresses; the state had its officials and families their household rules—yet even in the classics the number of truly exemplary men and women can still be counted on one's fingers.

sentences.zh: 世道既降，教典非古，男子之誌四方，猶可隆師親友以為善；

translations.literal: As the age declined and educational canons ceased to be ancient, a man who set his ambitions on the four quarters could still honor teachers and befriend the worthy to pursue goodness;
translations.idiomatic: As the world declined and educational standards fell away from antiquity, a man who traveled far could still seek out worthy teachers and friends to cultivate virtue;

sentences.zh: 女子生長環堵之中，能著美行垂於汗青，豈易得哉。

translations.literal: A woman who grew up within the four walls of a room and could achieve fine conduct recorded in the annals—how could that be easily attained?
translations.idiomatic: for a woman raised within the confines of the home to achieve conduct worthy of the historical record—how rare is that?

sentences.zh: 故曆代所傳列女，何可棄也？

translations.literal: Therefore the exemplary women transmitted through successive dynasties—how could they be discarded?
translations.idiomatic: How then could the exemplary women handed down through the ages ever be set aside?

sentences.zh: 考宋舊史得列女若幹人，作《列女傳》。

translations.literal: Examining the old histories of Song, I found a number of exemplary women and composed the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the old Song histories, I found a number of such women and have composed the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》.

sentences.zh: 朱娥者，越州上虞朱回女也。

translations.literal: Zhu E was the daughter of Zhu Hui of Shangyu in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu E was the daughter of Zhu Hui of Shangyu in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 母早亡，養於祖媼。

translations.literal: Her mother died early, and she was raised by her paternal grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother died when she was young, and she was raised by her grandmother.

sentences.zh: 娥十歲，裏中朱顏與媼競，持刀欲殺媼，一家驚潰，獨娥號呼突前，擁蔽其媼，手挽顏衣，以身下墜顏刀，曰：“寧殺我，毋殺媼也。

translations.literal: When E was ten, Zhu Yan of the neighborhood quarreled with the old woman, drew a knife intending to kill her; the whole household fled in panic. E alone cried out and rushed forward, shielding her grandmother, clutching Yan's garment and throwing herself beneath Yan's blade, saying: 'Better kill me—do not kill Grandmother.'
translations.idiomatic: When E was ten, a neighbor named Zhu Yan quarreled with her grandmother and drew a knife to kill her. The whole household fled in panic, but E alone cried out and rushed forward, shielding her grandmother, clutching Yan's robe and throwing herself beneath his blade. 'Kill me instead,' she cried, 'but spare Grandmother!'

sentences.zh: ”媼以娥故得脫。

translations.literal: The old woman escaped because of E.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to E, her grandmother escaped.

sentences.zh: 娥連被數十刀，猶手挽顏衣不釋，顏忿恚，斷其喉以死。

translations.literal: E suffered dozens of cuts in succession yet still clutched Yan's garment without releasing it. Yan, enraged, severed her throat and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: E was struck dozens of times yet still would not let go of Yan's robe. Enraged, Yan cut her throat and killed her.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜其家粟帛。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court bestowed grain and silk on her family.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, her family was granted grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 其後，會稽令董皆為娥立像於曹娥廟，歲時配享焉。

translations.literal: Later, Dong Jie, magistrate of Kuaiji, erected a statue of E in the Cao E Temple, where she received seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Dong Jie, magistrate of Kuaiji, erected a statue of her in the Cao E Temple, where she received sacrifices at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 張氏，鄂州江夏民婦。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi was a commoner's wife of Jiangxia in E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi was a commoner's wife from Jiangxia in Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 裏惡少謝師乞過其家，持刀逼欲與為亂，曰：“從我則全，不從則死。

translations.literal: A neighborhood ruffian, Xie Shiji, passed her home, drew a knife and pressed her to submit to debauchery, saying: 'Follow me and you shall live; refuse and you die.'
translations.idiomatic: A neighborhood ruffian named Xie Shiji passed her home, drew a knife, and tried to force himself on her. 'Do as I say and you live,' he said; 'refuse and you die.'

sentences.zh: ”張大罵曰：“庸奴！

translations.literal: Zhang cursed him loudly: 'Worthless slave!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang cursed him loudly: 'Worthless cur!

sentences.zh: 可死，不可它也。

translations.literal: I can die, but I cannot do otherwise.'
translations.idiomatic: I can die, but I will never yield to you.'

sentences.zh: ”至以刃斷其喉，猶能走，擒師乞，以告鄰人。

translations.literal: He cut her throat with the blade, yet she could still run, seized Shiji, and reported him to the neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: He slashed her throat, yet she still managed to run, seize Shiji, and turn him over to the neighbors.

sentences.zh: 既死，朝廷聞之，詔封旌德縣君，表墳曰“列女之墓”，賜酒帛，令郡縣致奠。

translations.literal: After her death the court heard of it and issued an edict enfeoffing her as Lady of Jingde County, marking her tomb 'Tomb of an Exemplary Woman,' bestowing wine and silk, and ordering the prefecture and county to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After her death the court learned of her deed and enfeoffed her posthumously as Lady of Jingde County, marked her tomb 'Tomb of an Exemplary Woman,' granted wine and silk, and ordered the local officials to perform sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 彭列女，生洪州分寧農家。

translations.literal: Peng Lienu was born into a farming family of Fenning in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Lienu was born into a farming family in Fenning, Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從父泰入山伐薪，父遇虎，將不脫，女拔刀斫虎，奪其父而還。

translations.literal: Her father's younger brother Tai entered the mountains to gather firewood; her father encountered a tiger and could not escape. The girl drew a knife, hacked at the tiger, seized her father, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Tai went into the mountains to gather firewood when her father encountered a tiger and could not escape. The girl drew a knife, hacked at the tiger, rescued her father, and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔賜粟帛，敕州縣歲時存問。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict granted grain and silk and ordered the prefecture and county to inquire after her welfare at the seasonal festivals.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, she was granted grain and silk, and the local officials were ordered to visit her family at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 郝節娥，嘉州娼家女。

translations.literal: Hao Jiee was the daughter of a courtesan's household in Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Jiee was born into a courtesan's household in Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 生五歲，母娼苦貧，賣於洪雅良家為養女。

translations.literal: At age five, her mother the courtesan, suffering poverty, sold her to a respectable family in Hongya as a foster daughter.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of five, her mother, struggling in poverty, sold her to a respectable family in Hongya to be raised as their daughter.

sentences.zh: 始笄，母奪而歸，欲令世其娼，娥不樂娼，日逼之，娥曰：“少育良家，習織作組紃之事，又輒精巧，粗可以給母朝夕，欲求此身使終為良，可乎？

translations.literal: When she first pinned up her hair, her mother seized her and took her back, wishing to make her inherit the courtesan's trade. E disliked the courtesan's life; day by day her mother pressed her. E said: 'Raised young in a respectable household, I learned weaving and braiding, and am always skillful at it—roughly enough to provide for Mother's daily needs. I wish to keep this body so that I may always remain respectable—is that possible?'
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age, her mother took her back, intending to pass on the courtesan's trade. E refused. Day after day her mother pressed her, until E said: 'I was raised from childhood in a respectable home and learned weaving and needlework, at which I am quite skilled—enough at least to provide for your daily needs. Cannot I keep this body respectable to the end?'

sentences.zh: ”母益怒，且箠且罵。

translations.literal: Her mother grew angrier still, beating and cursing her by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother only grew angrier, beating and cursing her in turn.

sentences.zh: 洪雅春時為蠶叢祠，娼與邑少年期，因蠶叢具酒邀娥。

translations.literal: In spring Hongya held sacrifices to the Silkworm God; the courtesan made an appointment with the young men of the district and, using the Silkworm God festival as pretext, prepared wine and invited E.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring Hongya held sacrifices to the Silkworm God. The courtesan arranged a meeting with the young men of the town and, using the festival as a pretext, prepared wine and invited E.

sentences.zh: 娼與娥徐往，娥見少年，倉皇驚走，母挽捽不使去。

translations.literal: The courtesan and E went slowly; when E saw the young men she fled in panic, but her mother seized and dragged her, not letting her leave.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and daughter went together. When E saw the young men she fled in panic, but her mother seized her and would not let her go.

sentences.zh: 不得已留坐中，時時顧酒食輒唾，強飲之，則嘔噦滿地，少年卒不得侵淩。

translations.literal: Unable to avoid it, she remained seated among them; whenever she glanced at food or drink she spat upon it, and when forced to drink she vomited all over the ground—the young men in the end could not molest her.
translations.idiomatic: Forced to stay, she spat on every dish and cup set before her, and when made to drink she vomited all over the floor. In the end the young men could not lay a hand on her.

sentences.zh: 暮歸，過雞鳴渡，娥度他日必不可脫，陽渴求飲，自投於江以死。

translations.literal: Returning at dusk, they passed Jiming Ford. E judged that another day she could not escape; feigning thirst she begged for drink and threw herself into the river to die.
translations.idiomatic: Returning at dusk, they passed Jiming Ford. E knew she could not escape forever; feigning thirst she asked for water and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 鄉人謂之“節娥”雲。

translations.literal: The people of the district called her 'Chaste E.'
translations.idiomatic: The people of the district called her 'Chaste E.'

sentences.zh: 朱氏，開封民婦也。

translations.literal: Zhu Shi was a commoner's wife of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shi was a commoner's wife in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 家貧，賣巾屨簪珥以給其夫。

translations.literal: The family was poor; she sold kerchiefs, shoes, hairpins, and earrings to provide for her husband.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, and she sold kerchiefs, shoes, hairpins, and earrings to support her husband.

sentences.zh: 夫日與俠少飲博，不以家為事，犯法徒武昌。

translations.literal: Her husband daily drank and gambled with ruffians, paid no heed to the household, broke the law, and was banished to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband spent his days drinking and gambling with ruffians, neglected the household, broke the law, and was exiled to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 父母欲奪而嫁之，朱曰：“何迫我如是耶？

translations.literal: Her parents wished to take her back and marry her off elsewhere. Zhu said: 'Why press me so harshly?'
translations.idiomatic: Her parents wished to take her back and marry her to another man. Zhu said: 'Why do you press me so?'

sentences.zh: ”其夫將行，一夕自經死，且曰：“及吾夫未去，使知我不為不義屈也。

translations.literal: On the eve of her husband's departure she hanged herself, saying: 'While my husband has not yet left, let him know that I will not yield to what is unrighteous.'
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of her husband's departure she hanged herself, leaving word: 'Before my husband leaves, let him know that I would never submit to what is unrighteous.'

sentences.zh: ”吳充時為開封府判官，作《阿朱詩》以道其事。

translations.literal: Wu Chong, then an assistant magistrate of the Kaifeng prefectural government, composed the 《Poem on Ah-Zhu》 to relate her story.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong, then an assistant magistrate in Kaifeng, composed the 《Poem on Ah-Zhu》 to commemorate her story.

sentences.zh: 崔氏，合淝包繶妻。

translations.literal: Cui Shi was the wife of Bao Ji of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi was the wife of Bao Ji of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 繶，樞密副使拯之子，早亡，惟一稚兒。

translations.literal: Ji was the son of Bao Zheng, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he died young, leaving only one infant son.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was the son of Bao Zheng, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He died young, leaving only one infant son.

sentences.zh: 拯夫婦意崔不能守也，使左右嚐其心。

translations.literal: Zheng and his wife suspected that Cui could not remain chaste and sent attendants to test her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and his wife doubted that Cui could remain faithful and sent attendants to test her resolve.

sentences.zh: 崔蓬垢涕泣出堂下，見拯曰：“翁，天下名公也。

translations.literal: Cui, disheveled and weeping, came out below the hall and saw Zheng, saying: 'Father-in-law, you are a renowned statesman of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Cui came out below the hall, disheveled and weeping, and said to Zheng: 'Father-in-law, you are a renowned statesman of the realm.

sentences.zh: 婦得齒賤獲，執瀚滌之事幸矣，況敢汙家乎！

translations.literal: Your daughter-in-law ranks with the meanest servants—fortunate merely to perform menial washing—how much less dare I defile the family!
translations.idiomatic: Your daughter-in-law ranks no higher than the meanest servant—fortunate only to perform menial chores—how could I dare bring shame upon this house!

sentences.zh: 生為包婦，死為包鬼，誓無它也。

translations.literal: Alive I am a wife of the Bao clan; dead I shall be a ghost of the Bao clan—I swear there shall be no other.'
translations.idiomatic: Alive I am a Bao wife; dead I shall be a Bao ghost—I swear there shall be no other.'

sentences.zh: 其後，稚兒亦卒。

translations.literal: Later the infant son also died.
translations.idiomatic: Later the infant son also died.

sentences.zh: 母呂自荊州來，誘崔欲嫁其族人，因謂曰：“喪夫守子，子死孰守？

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law Lü came from Jing Prefecture, tempted Cui to marry a kinsman of her own clan, and said: 'You mourned your husband and guarded your son—your son is dead; what is there left to guard?'
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law Lü came from Jingzhou and tried to persuade Cui to marry one of her own clansmen, saying: 'You mourned your husband and guarded your son—but your son is dead. What is left to guard?'

sentences.zh: ”崔曰：“昔之留也，非以子也，舅姑故也。

translations.literal: Cui said: 'When I remained before, it was not for the sake of the son—it was for my parents-in-law.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui replied: 'When I stayed before, it was not for my son—it was for my parents-in-law.'

sentences.zh: 今舅歿，姑老矣，將舍而去乎？

translations.literal: Now my father-in-law is dead and my mother-in-law is old—shall I abandon her and leave?'
translations.idiomatic: Now my father-in-law is dead and my mother-in-law is old—shall I abandon her and go?'

sentences.zh: ”呂怒，詛罵曰：“我寧死此，決不獨歸，須爾同往也。

translations.literal: Lü grew angry and cursed her: 'I would rather die here than return alone—you must go with me.'
translations.idiomatic: Lü grew angry and cursed her: 'I would rather die here than return alone—you must come with me.'

sentences.zh: ”崔泣曰：“母遠來，義不當使母獨還。

translations.literal: Cui wept and said: 'Mother has come from afar—it would not be right to let Mother return alone.
translations.idiomatic: Cui wept and said: 'Mother has come from far away—it would not be right to let you return alone.

sentences.zh: 然到荊州儻以不義見迫，必絕於尺組之下，願以屍還包氏。

translations.literal: Yet if in Jing Prefecture I am forced by what is unrighteous, I shall surely end my life beneath a length of cord and wish that my corpse be returned to the Bao clan.'
translations.idiomatic: But if in Jingzhou I am forced to what is unrighteous, I shall end my life by the cord and ask that my body be returned to the Bao clan.'

sentences.zh: ” 遂偕去。

translations.literal: They then went together.
translations.idiomatic: They then set out together.

sentences.zh: 母見其誓必死，卒還包氏。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law, seeing that her oath meant certain death, in the end returned her to the Bao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that her oath meant she would surely die, her mother-in-law in the end sent her back to the Bao household.

sentences.zh: 趙氏，貝州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shi was a native of Bei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shi was from Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 父嚐舉學究。

translations.literal: Her father had once passed the licentiate examination.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had once passed the licentiate examination.

sentences.zh: 王則反，聞趙氏有殊色，使人劫致之，欲納為妻。

translations.literal: When Wang Ze rebelled, hearing that Zhao Shi possessed extraordinary beauty, he sent men to seize her by force and wished to take her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze rebelled, he heard that Zhao Shi was exceptionally beautiful, sent men to seize her, and wished to take her as his wife.

sentences.zh: 趙日號哭慢罵求死，賊愛其色不殺，多使人守之。

translations.literal: Zhao daily wailed, cursed, and begged for death. The rebels, loving her beauty, did not kill her but set many men to guard her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao wailed and cursed day after day, begging for death. The rebels, captivated by her beauty, would not kill her but set many guards over her.

sentences.zh: 趙知不脫，乃紿曰：“必欲妻我，宜擇日以禮聘。

translations.literal: Zhao knew she could not escape and therefore deceived them, saying: 'If you must take me as wife, you should choose an auspicious day and betroth me with proper ceremony.'
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not escape, Zhao deceived them: 'If you must marry me, choose an auspicious day and betroth me with proper ceremony.'

sentences.zh: ”賊信之，使歸其家。

translations.literal: The rebels believed her and sent her back to her family.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels believed her and sent her home.

sentences.zh: 家人懼其自殞，得禍於賊，益使人守視。

translations.literal: Her family, fearing she would kill herself and bring disaster from the rebels, set even more people to watch over her.
translations.idiomatic: Her family, fearing she would kill herself and bring the rebels' wrath upon them, set even more guards to watch her.

sentences.zh: 賊具聘帛，盛輿從來迎。

translations.literal: The rebels prepared betrothal gifts and silks and came in grand procession with sedan chairs to welcome her.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels prepared betrothal gifts and came in grand procession with sedan chairs to fetch her.

sentences.zh: 趙與家人訣曰：“吾不復歸此矣。

translations.literal: Zhao took leave of her family, saying: 'I shall not return here again.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao bade her family farewell: 'I shall not return here again.'

sentences.zh: ”問其故，答曰：“豈有為賊汙辱至此，而尚有生理乎！

translations.literal: When they asked the reason, she answered: 'How could one who has been defiled by rebels to this degree still have any desire to live!'
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, she answered: 'How could one defiled by rebels to this degree still wish to live!'

sentences.zh: ”家人曰：“汝忍不為家族計？

translations.literal: Her family said: 'Can you bear not to consider the clan?'
translations.idiomatic: Her family said: 'Can you bear not to think of the family?'

sentences.zh: ”趙曰：“第亡患。

translations.literal: Zhao said: 'Just do not worry.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said: 'Do not worry.'

sentences.zh: ”遂涕泣登輿而去。

translations.literal: She then wept, mounted the sedan chair, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she mounted the sedan chair and departed.

sentences.zh: 至州廨，舉簾視之，已自縊輿中死矣。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefectural offices, they lifted the curtain to look at her—she had already hanged herself within the sedan chair and was dead.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the prefectural offices and lifted the curtain, she had already hanged herself in the sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 尚書屯田員外郎張寅有《趙女詩》。

translations.literal: Zhang Yin, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Field Office, composed the 《Poem on the Zhao Girl》.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Field Office, composed the 《Poem on the Zhao Girl》.

sentences.zh: 張晉卿妻丁氏，鄭州新鄭人，參知政事度五世孫也。

translations.literal: Ding Shi, wife of Zhang Jinqing, was a native of Xinzheng in Zheng Prefecture and a fifth-generation descendant of the Vice Councilor of State Du.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shi, wife of Zhang Jinqing, was from Xinzheng in Zhengzhou and a fifth-generation descendant of the Vice Councilor Du.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，與晉卿避金兵於大隗山。

translations.literal: During the Jingkang era she and Jinqing fled the Jin troops to Mount Dawei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang crisis she and Jinqing fled the Jin troops to Mount Dawei.

sentences.zh: 金兵入山，為所得，挾之鞍上。

translations.literal: Jin troops entered the mountain; she was seized and placed upon a saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops entered the mountain, seized her, and placed her upon a saddle.

sentences.zh: 丁自投於地，戟手大罵，連呼曰：“我死即死耳，誓不受辱於爾輩。

translations.literal: Ding threw herself to the ground, pointed her finger and cursed loudly, crying repeatedly: 'If I must die, then let me die—I swear I shall not suffer disgrace at your hands.'
translations.idiomatic: Ding threw herself to the ground, pointed her finger, and cursed them loudly: 'If I must die, then let me die—I swear I shall never suffer disgrace at your hands!'

sentences.zh: ”復挾上馬，再三罵不已。

translations.literal: They seized her onto the horse again; she cursed them again and again without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They seized her back onto the horse, but she cursed them again and again without cease.

sentences.zh: 卒乃忿然舉梃縱擊，遂死杖下。

translations.literal: At last, enraged, they raised clubs and beat her freely; she died beneath the cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: At last, enraged, they beat her with clubs until she died.

sentences.zh: 項氏，吉州吉水人。

translations.literal: Xiang Shi was a native of Jishui in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shi was from Jishui in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 居永昌裏，適同裏孫氏。

translations.literal: She lived on Yongchang Lane and married into the Sun clan of the same lane.
translations.idiomatic: She lived on Yongchang Lane and married a man of the Sun clan on the same lane.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，為裏胥所逮，至中途欲侵淩之，項引刀自刺而死。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe she was seized by the lane headman; midway he wished to molest her. Xiang drew a knife and stabbed herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuanhe she was seized by the lane headman, who tried to molest her on the way. Xiang drew a knife and stabbed herself to death.

sentences.zh: 郡以聞，詔贈孺人，旌表其廬。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported it; an edict posthumously granted her the title of Lady and marked her dwelling with a commemorative tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported her deed; the court posthumously granted her the title of Lady and marked her home with a commemorative tablet.

sentences.zh: 王氏二婦，汝州人。

translations.literal: The two wives of the Wang clan were natives of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The two Wang wives were from Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，金人至汝州，二婦為所掠，擁置舟中，遂投漢江以死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan the Jin reached Ru Prefecture; the two wives were seized, crowded into a boat, and threw themselves into the Han River to die.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyan era the Jin reached Ruzhou. The two wives were seized and crowded into a boat, whereupon they threw themselves into the Han River.

sentences.zh: 屍皆浮出不壞，人為收葬之城外江上，為雙塚以表之。

translations.literal: Their corpses all floated up uncorrupted; people collected and buried them outside the city on the riverbank, erecting twin mounds to commemorate them.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies floated up uncorrupted; the people buried them on the riverbank outside the city and erected twin mounds to commemorate them.

sentences.zh: 徐氏，和州人。

translations.literal: Xu Shi was a native of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shi was from Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 閎中女也，適同郡張弼。

translations.literal: She was the daughter of Hongzhong and married Zhang Bi of the same prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She was the daughter of Hongzhong and married Zhang Bi of the same prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年春，金人犯惟揚，官軍望風奔潰，多肆虜掠，執徐欲汙之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Jianyan the Jin invaded Huaiyang; government troops fled at the mere sight of them, and many plundered freely. They seized Xu and wished to defile her.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Jianyan the Jin invaded Huaiyang. Government troops fled at the mere sight of them, and many took to plundering. They seized Xu and tried to violate her.

sentences.zh: 徐瞋目大罵曰：“朝廷蓄汝輩以備緩急，今敵犯行在，既不能赴難，又乘時為盜，我恨一女子不能引劍斷汝頭，以快眾憤，肯為汝辱以苟活耶！

translations.literal: Xu glared and cursed loudly: 'The court nurtured you to meet emergencies—now the enemy violates the imperial residence, yet you cannot rush to the crisis and instead seize the moment to become robbers! I regret that as a mere woman I cannot draw a sword and sever your heads to satisfy the people's wrath—would I submit to your disgrace merely to cling to life!'
translations.idiomatic: Xu glared and cursed them: 'The court nurtured you for times of emergency—yet when the enemy threatens the imperial residence you cannot rush to its defense and instead take to robbery! I regret that as a mere woman I cannot draw a sword and cut off your heads to satisfy the people's wrath—do you think I would submit to your disgrace merely to cling to life!'

sentences.zh: 第速殺我。

translations.literal: Just kill me quickly.'
translations.idiomatic: Just kill me quickly.'

sentences.zh: ”賊慚恚，以刃刺殺之，投江中而去。

translations.literal: The bandits, ashamed and enraged, stabbed and killed her with blades and cast her into the river before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and enraged, the bandits stabbed her to death and cast her body into the river.

sentences.zh: 榮氏，薿女弟也。

translations.literal: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Shi was the younger sister of Rong.

sentences.zh: 自幼如成人，讀《論語》、《孝經》，能通大義，事父母孝。

translations.literal: From childhood she was like an adult; she read the 《Analects》 and 《Classic of Filial Piety》, understood their great principles, and served her parents with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was precocious; she read the 《Analects》 and 《Classic of Filial Piety》, grasped their essential teachings, and served her parents with devotion.

sentences.zh: 歸將作監主簿馬元穎。

translations.literal: She married Ma Yuanying, Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: She married Ma Yuanying, Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，賊張遇寇儀真，榮與其姑及二女走惟揚，姑素羸，榮扶掖不忍舍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan the bandit Zhang Yu raided Yizhen; Rong fled with her mother-in-law and two daughters toward Huaiyang. Her mother-in-law had always been frail; Rong supported and guided her, unwilling to abandon her.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan the bandit Zhang Yu raided Yizhen. Rong fled with her mother-in-law and two daughters toward Huaiyang. Her mother-in-law had always been frail, and Rong supported her, unwilling to leave her behind.

sentences.zh: 俄賊至，脅之不從，賊殺其女，脅之益急，榮厲聲詬罵，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Soon the bandits arrived; she refused their threats. The bandits killed her daughters; their threats grew more urgent. Rong cursed them in a fierce voice and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bandits arrived. She refused their demands; they killed her daughters and pressed her harder. Rong cursed them in a fierce voice and was killed.

sentences.zh: 何氏，吳人。

translations.literal: He Shi was a native of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He Shi was from Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳永年之妻也。

translations.literal: She was the wife of Wu Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: She was the wife of Wu Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年春，金兵道三吳，官兵遁去，城中人死者五十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Jianyan Jin troops passed through the Three Wu regions; government troops fled, and more than five hundred thousand people in the cities died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year of Jianyan Jin troops passed through the Three Wu regions. Government troops fled, and more than five hundred thousand people in the cities perished.

sentences.zh: 永年與其姊及其妻何奉母而逃。

translations.literal: Yongnian fled with his elder sister and his wife He, supporting their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yongnian fled with his elder sister and his wife He, supporting their mother as they went.

sentences.zh: 母老，待挾持而行，卒為賊所得，將縶其姊及何，何紿謂賊曰：“諸君何不武耶！

translations.literal: Her mother was old and had to be supported as they walked; in the end they were seized by bandits, who were about to bind her elder sister and He. He deceived the bandits, saying: "Why are you all so unmanly!
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was elderly and had to be helped along; in the end they were seized by bandits, who were about to bind her elder sister and He. He deceived the bandits: "Why are you so unmanly!

sentences.zh: 婦人東西惟命爾。

translations.literal: A woman's east and west are at your command alone."
translations.idiomatic: A woman goes where you command—that is all."

sentences.zh: ”賊信之。

translations.literal: The bandits believed her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits believed her.

sentences.zh: 行次水濱，謂其夫曰：“我不負君。

translations.literal: Midway beside the water she said to her husband: "I shall not fail you."
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the riverbank she said to her husband: "I shall not fail you."

sentences.zh: ”遂投於河，其姊繼之。

translations.literal: She then threw herself into the river, and her elder sister followed.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the river, and her elder sister followed.

sentences.zh: 董氏，沂州滕縣人，許適劉氏子。

translations.literal: Dong Shi was a native of Teng County in Yi Prefecture and was betrothed to a son of the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shi was from Teng County in Yizhou and was betrothed to a son of the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，盜李昱攻剽滕縣，悅其色，欲亂之，誘諭再三，曰：“汝不我從，當剉汝萬段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan the bandit Li Yu raided Teng County, delighted by her beauty and wishing to violate her; he tempted and persuaded her again and again, saying: "If you do not follow me, I shall cut you into ten thousand pieces."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyan the bandit Li Yu raided Teng County. Captivated by her beauty, he tried to violate her, tempting and threatening her again and again: "Follow me or I shall cut you into ten thousand pieces."

sentences.zh: ”女終不屈，遂斷其首。

translations.literal: The girl in the end would not yield, so he cut off her head.
translations.idiomatic: She refused to the end, and he cut off her head.

sentences.zh: 劉氏子聞女死狀，大慟曰：“列女也。

translations.literal: The son of the Liu clan, hearing how the girl died, wailed greatly and said: "An exemplary woman."
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clansman, hearing how she died, wailed and said: "A true exemplary woman."

sentences.zh: ”葬之，為立祠。

translations.literal: He buried her and erected a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He buried her and built a shrine in her honor.

sentences.zh: 三年春，盜馬進掠臨淮縣，王宣要其妻曹氏避之，曹曰：“我聞婦人死不出閨房。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, the bandit Ma Jin raided Linhuai County; Wang Xuan asked his wife Cao Shi to flee with him. Cao said: "I have heard that a woman in death does not leave her chamber."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the bandit Ma Jin raided Linhuai County. Wang Xuan asked his wife Cao to flee with him, but Cao said: "I have heard that a virtuous woman does not leave her chamber even in death."

sentences.zh: ”賊至，宣避之，曹堅臥不起。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, Xuan fled; Cao lay firm in bed and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, Xuan fled, but Cao lay firm in bed and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 眾賊劫持之，大罵不屈，為所害。

translations.literal: The bandits seized and dragged her; she cursed them loudly without yielding and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized her; she cursed them without yielding and was killed.

sentences.zh: 四年，盜祝友聚眾於滁州龔家城，掠人為糧。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the bandit Zhu You gathered a crowd at the Gong family fort in Chuzhou and seized people for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the bandit Zhu You gathered followers at the Gong family fort in Chuzhou and seized people for food.

sentences.zh: 東安縣民丁國兵者及其妻為友所掠，妻泣曰：“丁氏族流亡已盡，乞存夫以續其祀。

translations.literal: A man of Dong'an County named Ding Guobing and his wife were seized by You. The wife wept and said: "The Ding clan's exiles are already gone—please spare my husband to continue his sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Guobing of Dong'an County and his wife were seized by You. His wife wept: "The Ding clan's exiles are already gone—please spare my husband to continue the family line."

sentences.zh: ”賊遂釋夫而害之。

translations.literal: The bandits then released the husband and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released the husband and killed her.

sentences.zh: 同時，叛卒楊寇南劍州，道出小常村，掠一民婦，欲與亂，婦毅然誓死不受汙，遂遇害，棄屍道傍。

translations.literal: At the same time the mutineer Yang Kou passed through Nanjian Prefecture by way of Xiaochang Village, seized a commoner's wife, and wished to violate her; the woman resolutely swore to die rather than suffer defilement, was killed, and her corpse was cast beside the road.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the mutineer Yang Kou passed through Nanjian Prefecture via Xiaochang Village, seized a commoner's wife, and tried to violate her. She swore to die rather than be defiled, was killed, and her body was cast beside the road.

sentences.zh: 賊退，人為收瘞。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated, people collected and buried her.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits retreated, the people buried her.

sentences.zh: 屍所枕藉處，跡宛然不滅。

translations.literal: Where the corpse had lain upon the ground, the trace remained distinct and undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: Where her body had lain, the imprint on the ground remained distinct and undiminished.

sentences.zh: 每雨則幹，睛則濕，則削去即復見。

translations.literal: Whenever it rained it dried; when clear it grew damp—if scraped away it reappeared.
translations.idiomatic: When it rained the mark dried; when the sky cleared it grew damp again—and if scraped away, it reappeared.

sentences.zh: 覆以他土，其跡愈明。

translations.literal: If covered with other earth, the trace grew even clearer.
translations.idiomatic: If covered with other earth, the imprint grew even clearer.

sentences.zh: 譚氏，英州真陽縣人，曲江村士人吳琪妻也。

translations.literal: Tan Shi was a native of Zhenyang County in Ying Prefecture and the wife of the village scholar Wu Qi of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shi was from Zhenyang County in Yingzhou and the wife of the village scholar Wu Qi of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，英州饑，觀音山盜起，攻剽鄉落。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, Ying Prefecture suffered famine and bandits rose on Guanyin Mountain, raiding the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Shaoxing Yingzhou suffered famine and bandits rose on Guanyin Mountain, raiding the countryside.

sentences.zh: 琪竄去，譚不能俱，與其女被執。

translations.literal: Qi fled; Tan could not go with him and was seized together with her daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fled; Tan could not accompany him and was seized together with her daughter.

sentences.zh: 譚有姿色，盜欲妻之，譚怒罵曰：“爾輩賊也。

translations.literal: Tan possessed beauty; the bandits wished to take her as wife. Tan cursed angrily: "You lot are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was beautiful; the bandits wished to marry her. She cursed them: "You are bandits.

sentences.zh: 我良家女，豈若偶耶？

translations.literal: I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I be your mate?"
translations.idiomatic: I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I wed you?"

sentences.zh: ”賊度無可奈何，害之。

translations.literal: The bandits judged that nothing could be done and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing there was nothing to be done, the bandits killed her.

sentences.zh: 同時，有南雄李科妻謝氏，保昌故村人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Xie Shi, wife of Li Ke of Nanxiong, from the old village of Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Xie Shi, wife of Li Ke of Nanxiong, from the old village of Baochang.

sentences.zh: 囚於虔盜中，數日，有欲犯之，謝唾其面目：“寧萬段我，不汝徇也。

translations.literal: Imprisoned among the bandits of Qian for several days, when some wished to violate her, Xie spat in their faces: "Better cut me into ten thousand pieces than have me submit to you."
translations.idiomatic: Held captive among the bandits of Qian for several days, when some tried to violate her, Xie spat in their faces: "Cut me into ten thousand pieces—I will never submit to you."

sentences.zh: ”盜怒，剉之而去。

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry, dismembered her, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits dismembered her and left.

sentences.zh: 劉氏，海州朐山人，適同裏陳公緒。

translations.literal: Liu Shi was a native of Qushan in Haizhou and married Chen Gongxu of the same lane.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi was from Qushan in Haizhou and married Chen Gongxu of the same neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 紹興末，金人犯山東，郡縣震響，公緒倡義來歸，偶劉歸寧，倉卒不得與偕，惟挈其子庚以行，宋授以八品官，後累功至正使。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin invaded Shandong; prefectures and counties trembled. Gongxu raised righteous arms and came over to the Song; by chance Liu returned home to visit her parents and in the haste could not go with him—he took only their son Geng. The Song granted him an eighth-rank post; later, through accumulated merit, he rose to Regular Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shaoxing era the Jin invaded Shandong and the region was in turmoil. Gongxu raised a loyal force and submitted to the Song. Liu happened to be visiting her parents and could not leave with him in the haste—he took only their son Geng. The Song granted him an eighth-rank post; through accumulated merit he later rose to Regular Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 劉留北方，音問不通。

translations.literal: Liu remained in the north; letters and inquiries could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu remained in the north; no word could reach her.

sentences.zh: 或語之曰：“人言‘貴易交，富易妻’。

translations.literal: Some said to her: "People say, 'When one grows noble, friendships change; when one grows rich, wives change.'"
translations.idiomatic: Some told her: "People say that when a man grows noble his friendships change, and when he grows rich he changes his wife."

sentences.zh: 今陳已貴，必他娶矣，盍改適？

translations.literal: "Now Chen has grown eminent—he must have taken another wife. Why not remarry?"
translations.idiomatic: "Chen is now eminent—he must have remarried. Why not marry again?"

sentences.zh: ”曰：“吾知守吾誌而已，皇恤乎他？

translations.literal: She said: "I know only to keep to my resolve—why should I fear anything else?"
translations.idiomatic: She said: "I know only to keep my resolve—why should I fear anything else?"

sentences.zh: ”公緒亦不他娶。

translations.literal: Gongxu likewise did not take another wife.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxu likewise never remarried.

sentences.zh: 子庚浸長，輒思念涕泣，傾家貲，結任俠，奔走淮甸，險阻備嚐。

translations.literal: As Geng gradually grew, he often thought of her and wept; he spent the family fortune, joined with bold knights-errant, and rushed about the Huai region, tasting every hardship and danger.
translations.idiomatic: As Geng grew older he often thought of her and wept; he spent the family fortune, joined with bold adventurers, and traveled the Huai region through every hardship and danger.

sentences.zh: 如是者十餘年，遂得迎母以歸。

translations.literal: Thus for more than ten years, he was finally able to bring his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years of this, he was finally able to bring his mother home.

sentences.zh: 劉在北二十五年，嚐緯蕭以自給。

translations.literal: Liu had been in the north for twenty-five years and had always woven rush mats to support herself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had been in the north for twenty-five years, weaving rush mats to support herself.

sentences.zh: 張氏，羅江士人女。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi was the daughter of a scholar of Luojiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi was the daughter of a scholar of Luojiang.

sentences.zh: 其母楊氏寡居。

translations.literal: Her mother Yang Shi lived as a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother Yang Shi lived as a widow.

sentences.zh: 一日，親黨有婚會，母女偕往，其典庫雍乙者從行。

translations.literal: One day, kinsmen held a wedding feast; mother and daughter went together, and Yong Yi, the storehouse keeper, accompanied them.
translations.idiomatic: One day kinsmen held a wedding feast; mother and daughter went together, accompanied by Yong Yi, the storehouse keeper.

sentences.zh: 既就坐，乙先歸。

translations.literal: Once seated, Yi returned first.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were seated, Yi returned home first.

sentences.zh: 會罷，楊氏歸，則乙死於庫，莫知殺者主名。

translations.literal: When the feast ended, Yang returned and found Yi dead in the storehouse, with no knowing who had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended, Yang returned to find Yi dead in the storehouse, with no knowing who had killed him.

sentences.zh: 提點成都府路刑獄張文饒疑楊有私，懼為人知，殺乙以滅口，遂命石泉軍劾治。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenrao, Commissioner of Judicial Review for the Chengdu Circuit, suspected Yang of having a secret affair and, fearing exposure, killed Yi to silence him; he ordered Shiquan Army to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenrao, Commissioner of Judicial Review for the Chengdu Circuit, suspected Yang of a secret affair and, fearing exposure, of killing Yi to silence him; he ordered Shiquan to investigate.

sentences.zh: 楊言與女同榻，實無他。

translations.literal: Yang said she and her daughter shared a bed and there was truly nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Yang said she and her daughter shared a bed and there was truly nothing else.

sentences.zh: 遂逮其女，考掠無實。

translations.literal: They then seized the daughter; torture yielded no confession.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized the daughter; torture yielded no confession.

sentences.zh: 吏乃掘地為坑，縛母於其內，旁列熾火，間以水沃之，絕而復蘇者屢，辭終不服。

translations.literal: The clerks dug a pit in the earth, bound the mother within it, set blazing fires beside her, and intermittently poured water upon her; she died and revived repeatedly, yet her testimony never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks dug a pit, bound the mother inside, set fires blazing beside her, and intermittently poured water on her; she died and revived repeatedly, yet never confessed.

sentences.zh: 一日，女謂獄吏曰：“我不勝苦毒，將死矣，願一見母而絕。

translations.literal: One day the daughter said to the prison clerk: "I cannot bear this cruel torment and am about to die; let me see my mother once more and perish."
translations.idiomatic: One day the daughter told the prison clerk: "I cannot bear this torture and am about to die; let me see my mother once more."

sentences.zh: ”吏憐而許之。

translations.literal: The clerk pitied her and consented.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk pitied her and agreed.

sentences.zh: 既見，謂母曰：“母以清潔聞，奈何受此汙辱。

translations.literal: After seeing her, she said to her mother: "Mother is known for purity—how can you suffer this disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: When she saw her mother she said: "You are known for your purity—how can you suffer this disgrace?

sentences.zh: 寧死箠楚，不可自誣。

translations.literal: Better die under the rod than falsely incriminate yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Better die under the rod than falsely confess.

sentences.zh: 女今死，死將訟冤於天。

translations.literal: I shall die now, and in death I shall plead my grievance before Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I die now, and in death I shall plead my grievance before Heaven."

sentences.zh: ”言終而絕。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking, she expired.
translations.idiomatic: With these words she died.

sentences.zh: 於是石泉連三日地大震，有聲如雷，天雨雪，屋瓦皆落，邦人震恐。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shiquan for three days in succession suffered great earthquakes, sounds like thunder, sky rain mixed with snow, and roof tiles falling; the people were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shiquan suffered great earthquakes for three days, thunderous sounds, rain mixed with snow, and falling roof tiles; the people were terrified.

sentences.zh: 勘官李誌寧疑其獄，夕具衣冠禱於天。

translations.literal: The investigating official Li Zhiyuan doubted the case; in the evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating official Li Zhiyuan doubted the case; that evening he dressed in full regalia and prayed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 俄假寐坐廳事，恍有猿墜前，驚寤，呼吏卒索之，不見。

translations.literal: Soon, in a light sleep in the hall, he seemed to see an ape fall before him; startled awake, he called clerks and runners to search, but none was found.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, dozing in the hall, he seemed to see an ape fall before him; startled awake, he called his men to search, but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 誌寧自念夢兆：“非殺人者袁姓乎？

translations.literal: Zhiyuan thought to himself about the dream omen: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan reflected on the dream: "Is not the killer surnamed Yuan?"

sentences.zh: ”有門卒忽言張氏饋食之夫曰袁大，明日袁至，使吏執之，曰：“殺人者汝也。

translations.literal: A gate guard suddenly said the man who brought food to the Zhang household was called Yuan the Elder; the next day Yuan arrived, and he had the clerks seize him, saying: "You are the killer."
translations.idiomatic: A gate guard suddenly said the man who brought food to the Zhang household was called Yuan the Elder. The next day Yuan arrived; Li had him seized and said: "You are the killer."

sentences.zh: ”袁色動，遽曰：“吾憐之久矣，願就死。

translations.literal: Yuan's expression changed; he quickly said: "I have long pitied her—I am willing to die."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's expression changed; he quickly said: "I have long pitied her—I am willing to die."

sentences.zh: ”問之，云：“適盜庫金，會雍歸，遂殺之。

translations.literal: When questioned, he said: "I was stealing gold from the storehouse when Yong returned, so I killed him."
translations.idiomatic: Under questioning he said: "I was stealing gold from the storehouse when Yong returned, so I killed him."

sentences.zh: ”楊乃得免。

translations.literal: Yang was thereby exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was thereby exonerated.

sentences.zh: 時女死才數日也。

translations.literal: The girl had been dead only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: The girl had been dead only a few days.

sentences.zh: 獄上，郡榜其所居曰孝感坊。

translations.literal: When the case was reported upward, the prefecture posted a placard at her dwelling calling it the Lane of Filial Response.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, the prefecture posted a placard at her dwelling naming it the Lane of Filial Response.

sentences.zh: 師氏，彭州永豐人。

translations.literal: Shi Shi was a native of Yongfeng in Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi was from Yongfeng in Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父驥，政和二年省試第一。

translations.literal: Her father Ji ranked first in the provincial examination of the second year of Zhenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Ji ranked first in the provincial examination of the second year of Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 宣和中，為右正言十餘日，凡七八疏，論權幸及廉訪使者之害而去。

translations.literal: During the Xuanhe era he served as Right Remonstrator for more than ten days, in all seven or eight memorials criticizing powerful favorites and the harm done by investigation commissioners before departing office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuanhe era he served as Right Remonstrator for more than ten days, submitting seven or eight memorials criticizing powerful favorites and investigation commissioners before leaving office.

sentences.zh: 女適範世雍子孝純。

translations.literal: The daughter married Xiao Chun, son of Fan Shiyong.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter married Xiao Chun, son of Fan Shiyong.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，還蜀，至唐州方城縣，會賊朱顯終掠方城，孝純先被害，賊執師氏欲強之，許以不死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan they returned to Shu; reaching Fangcheng County in Tang Prefecture, they encountered the bandit Zhu Xianzhong raiding Fangcheng. Xiao Chun was killed first; the bandits seized Shi and wished to force her, promising her she would not die.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyan they returned to Shu. Reaching Fangcheng County in Tangzhou, they encountered the bandit Zhu Xianzhong raiding the county. Xiao Chun was killed first; the bandits seized Shi and tried to force her, promising she would not die.

sentences.zh: 師罵曰：“我中朝言官女，豈可受賊辱！

translations.literal: Shi cursed: "I am the daughter of a remonstrating official of the central court—how could I suffer disgrace at the hands of bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Shi cursed them: "I am the daughter of a remonstrating official of the central court—how could I suffer disgrace at bandits' hands!

sentences.zh: 吾夫已死，宜速殺我。

translations.literal: My husband is already dead—kill me quickly."
translations.idiomatic: My husband is already dead—kill me quickly."

sentences.zh: ”賊知不可屈，遂害之。

translations.literal: The bandits knew she could not be bent and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not be bent, the bandits killed her.

sentences.zh: 陳堂前，漢州雒縣王氏女。

translations.literal: Chen Tangqian was the daughter of the Wang clan of Luoxian in Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tangqian was the daughter of the Wang clan of Luoxian in Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 節操行義，為鄉人所敬，但呼曰“堂前”，猶私家尊其母也。

translations.literal: Her chastity, conduct, and righteousness won the respect of the district; people simply called her "Tangqian," as in a private household's respectful address for its mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her chastity, conduct, and righteousness won the respect of the district; people simply called her "Tangqian," as families respectfully address a mother.

sentences.zh: 堂前年十八，歸同郡陳安節，歲餘夫卒，僅有一子。

translations.literal: Tangqian was eighteen when she married Chen Anjie of the same prefecture; after a year and more her husband died, leaving only one son.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqian was eighteen when she married Chen Anjie of the same prefecture; after little more than a year her husband died, leaving only one son.

sentences.zh: 舅姑無生事，堂前斂泣告曰：“人之有子，在奉親克家爾。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law had no means of livelihood; Tangqian, restraining her tears, reported: "For people to have sons is to serve parents and sustain the household.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law had no means of support; Tangqian, holding back tears, said: "The purpose of having sons is to serve parents and sustain the household.

sentences.zh: 今已無可奈何，婦願幹蠱，如子在日。

translations.literal: Now there is nothing more to be done; your daughter-in-law wishes to manage affairs as though the son were still alive."
translations.idiomatic: That is no longer possible; your daughter-in-law wishes to manage affairs as though your son were still alive."

sentences.zh: ”舅姑曰：“若然，吾子不亡矣。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law said: "If so, our son is not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law said: "If so, our son is not dead."

sentences.zh: ”既葬其夫，事親治家有法，舅姑安之。

translations.literal: After burying her husband, she governed the household and served her elders by rule; her parents-in-law were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After burying her husband, she managed the household by proper methods and put her parents-in-law at ease.

sentences.zh: 子日新，年稍長，延名儒訓導，既冠，入太學，年三十卒。

translations.literal: Her son Rixin, as he gradually grew, was placed under renowned scholars for instruction; after coming of age he entered the Imperial College and died at thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Rixin, as he grew, was placed under renowned scholars; after coming of age he entered the Imperial College and died at thirty.

sentences.zh: 二孫曰綱曰紱，鹹篤學有聞。

translations.literal: Two grandsons, Gang and Fu, were both earnest in study and won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons, Gang and Fu, were both earnest scholars of renown.

sentences.zh: 初，堂前歸陳，夫之妹尚幼，堂前教育之，及笄，以厚禮嫁遣。

translations.literal: When Tangqian first married into the Chen family, her husband's younger sister was still young; Tangqian educated her, and when she came of age, sent her off in marriage with generous rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangqian first married into the Chen family, her husband's younger sister was still young; Tangqian educated her and, when she came of age, sent her off with generous marriage rites.

sentences.zh: 舅姑亡，妹求分財產，堂前盡遺室中所有，無靳色。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law died, the younger sister sought a division of property; Tangqian gave her everything in the house without a trace of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents-in-law died, the younger sister sought a division of property; Tangqian gave her everything in the house without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 不五年，妹所得財為夫所罄，乃歸悔。

translations.literal: Within five years the property the sister had received was exhausted by her husband, and she returned in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years her husband had exhausted the property, and she returned in regret.

sentences.zh: 堂前為買田置屋，撫育諸甥無異己子。

translations.literal: Tangqian bought fields and set up a house for her and reared her nephews no differently from her own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqian bought fields and a house for her and reared her nephews no differently from her own sons.

sentences.zh: 親屬有貧窶不能自存者，收養婚嫁至三四十人，自後宗族無慮百數。

translations.literal: Kinsmen too poor to support themselves—she took in, provided for, and married off as many as thirty or forty; afterward the clan numbered nearly a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen too poor to support themselves—she took in, provided for, and married off as many as thirty or forty; afterward the clan numbered nearly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 裏有故家甘氏，貧而質其季女於酒家，堂前出金贖之，俾有所歸。

translations.literal: In the lane was an old family, the Gan clan, poor and who had pawned their youngest daughter to a wine shop; Tangqian paid gold to redeem her and gave her a proper home.
translations.idiomatic: In the lane was an old family, the Gans, so poor they had pawned their youngest daughter to a wine shop; Tangqian paid gold to redeem her and gave her a proper home.

sentences.zh: 子孫遵其遺訓，五世同居，並以孝友儒業著聞。

translations.literal: Descendants followed her precepts; for five generations they dwelt together, all renowned for filial devotion, friendship, and Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants followed her teachings; for five generations they lived together, renowned for filial devotion, friendship, and Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，詔旌表其門閭雲。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, an edict marked her gate and lane with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qiandao an edict marked her gate and lane with commendation.

sentences.zh: 廖氏，臨江軍貢士歐陽希文之妻也。

translations.literal: Liao Shi was the wife of Ouyang Xiwen, a presented scholar of Linjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Shi was the wife of Ouyang Xiwen, a presented scholar of Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年春，盜起建昌，號“白氈笠”，過臨江，希文與妻共挾其母傅走山中，為賊所追。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Shaoxing, bandits rose in Jianchang, calling themselves "White Felt Hats"; passing through Linjiang, Xiwen and his wife together escorted their mother Fu into the mountains and were pursued by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Shaoxing bandits rose in Jianchang, calling themselves "White Felt Hats." Passing through Linjiang, Xiwen and his wife escorted their mother Fu into the mountains and were pursued by bandits.

sentences.zh: 廖以身蔽姑，使希文負之逃。

translations.literal: Liao shielded her mother-in-law with her body and had Xiwen carry her and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Liao shielded her mother-in-law with her body and had Xiwen carry her and flee.

sentences.zh: 賊執廖氏，廖正色叱之。

translations.literal: The bandits seized Liao; Liao sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits seized Liao; she sternly rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 賊知不可屈，揮刃斷其耳與臂，廖猶謂賊曰：“爾輩叛逆至此，我即死，爾輩亦不久屠戮。

translations.literal: The bandits knew she could not be bent; brandishing blades they cut off her ear and arm. Liao still said to the bandits: "You rebels have come to this—though I die, you too shall soon be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not be bent, the bandits cut off her ear and arm. Liao still told them: "You rebels have come to this—though I die, you too shall soon be slaughtered."

sentences.zh: ”語絕而仆。

translations.literal: When her words ended she collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: With these words she collapsed.

sentences.zh: 鄉人義而葬之，號“廖節婦墓”。

translations.literal: The villagers, moved by righteousness, buried her and called it the Tomb of the Chaste Wife Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her righteousness, the villagers buried her and called it the Tomb of the Chaste Wife Liao.

sentences.zh: 是年，盜彭友犯吉州龍泉，李生妻梁氏義不受辱，赴水而死。

translations.literal: That same year the bandit Peng You raided Longquan in Ji Prefecture; Li Sheng's wife Liang Shi, choosing righteousness, would not suffer disgrace and threw herself into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the bandit Peng You raised Longquan in Jizhou; Li Sheng's wife Liang Shi, choosing righteousness over disgrace, drowned herself in the river.

sentences.zh: 王氏，利州路提舉常平司幹辦公事劉當可之母也。

translations.literal: Wang Shi was the mother of Liu Dangke, Clerk of the Ever-Normal Granary Commission of Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi was the mother of Liu Dangke, Clerk of the Ever-Normal Granary Commission of Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年，就養興元。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoding she went to receive support at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaoding she went to Xingyuan to live under her son's support.

sentences.zh: 大元兵破蜀，提刑龐授檄當可詣行司議事。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army broke Shu; the judicial commissioner Pang Shou issued a dispatch summoning Dangke to the mobile headquarters to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army conquered Shu, Judicial Commissioner Pang Shou dispatched Liu Dangke to the mobile headquarters for consultation.

sentences.zh: 當可捧檄白母，王氏毅然勉之曰：“汝食君祿，豈可辭難。

translations.literal: Dangke received the dispatch and reported to his mother; Wang Shi resolutely encouraged him, saying: 'You eat the ruler's salary—how can you decline hardship?'
translations.idiomatic: Dangke received the dispatch and told his mother; Wang Shi resolutely urged him: 'You draw the ruler's salary—how can you shrink from hardship?'

sentences.zh: ”當可行，大元軍屠興元，王氏義不辱，大罵投江而死。

translations.literal: Dangke departed; the Great Yuan army massacred Xingyuan. Wang Shi, choosing righteousness over disgrace, cursed them loudly and threw herself into the river to die.
translations.idiomatic: Dangke set out; the Yuan army massacred Xingyuan. Wang Shi, choosing death over disgrace, cursed them and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 其婦杜氏及婢仆五人，鹹及於難。

translations.literal: His daughter-in-law Du Shi and five maidservants all perished in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter-in-law Du Shi and five maidservants all perished in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 當可聞變，奔赴江滸，得母喪以歸。

translations.literal: When Dangke heard of the disaster, he rushed to the riverbank, recovered his mother's body, and brought it home.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the disaster, Dangke rushed to the riverbank, recovered his mother's body, and brought it home.

sentences.zh: 詔贈和義郡太夫人。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted her the title of Grand Lady of Heyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted her the title of Grand Lady of Heyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾氏婦晏，汀州寧化人。

translations.literal: Yan, wife of the Zeng clan, was a native of Ninghua in Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, wife of the Zeng clan, was from Ninghua in Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫死，守幼子不嫁。

translations.literal: When her husband died, she guarded her young son and did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died, she guarded her young son and never remarried.

sentences.zh: 紹定間，寇破寧化縣，令佐俱逃，將樂縣宰黃垺令土豪王萬全、王倫結約諸砦以拒賊，晏首助兵給糧，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: During the Shaoding era bandits broke Ninghua County; the magistrate and assistants all fled. Huang Kun, magistrate of Jiangle County, ordered the local strongmen Wang Wanquan and Wang Lun to join the stockades in resisting the bandits; Yan was foremost in supplying troops and grain, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoding era bandits overran Ninghua County; officials all fled. Huang Kun, magistrate of Jiangle, organized local strongmen Wang Wanquan and Wang Lun to rally the stockades against the bandits; Yan was foremost in supplying troops and grain, and many enemies were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 賊忿其敗，結集愈眾，諸砦不能禦，晏乃依黃牛山傍，自為一砦。

translations.literal: The bandits, enraged at their defeat, gathered in ever greater numbers; the stockades could not withstand them. Yan then relied on the slopes of Yellow Ox Mountain and established a stockade of her own.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged at their defeats, the bandits gathered in greater numbers and the stockades could not hold. Yan then established her own stockade on Yellow Ox Mountain.

sentences.zh: 一日，賊遣數十人來索婦女金帛，晏召其田丁諭曰：“汝曹衣食我家，賊求婦女，意實在我。

translations.literal: One day the bandits sent several dozen men to demand women's gold and silks. Yan summoned her tenant farmers and instructed them: 'You all eat and clothe yourselves at my household's expense; when the bandits demand women, their intent is really upon me.
translations.idiomatic: One day the bandits sent dozens of men to demand women and valuables. Yan summoned her tenant farmers and said: 'You live at my household's expense; when they demand women, their target is really me.

sentences.zh: 汝念主母，各當用命，不勝即殺我。

translations.literal: Think of your mistress—each of you must fight with all your strength; if you cannot prevail, then kill me.'
translations.idiomatic: Think of your mistress—fight with all your strength; if you cannot win, then kill me.'

sentences.zh: ”因解首飾悉與田丁，田丁感激思奮。

translations.literal: She then removed her jewelry and gave it all to the tenant farmers; moved to gratitude, they resolved to fight fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: She removed her jewelry and gave it all to them; grateful, they resolved to fight fiercely.

sentences.zh: 晏自捶鼓，使諸婢鳴金，以作其勇。

translations.literal: Yan herself beat the drum and had the maidservants strike gongs to rouse their courage.
translations.idiomatic: Yan herself beat the drum while her maidservants struck gongs to rouse their courage.

sentences.zh: 賊復退敗。

translations.literal: The bandits were again driven back in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were driven back in defeat again.

sentences.zh: 鄰鄉知其可依，挈家依黃牛山避難者甚眾。

translations.literal: Neighboring districts, knowing they could rely on her, brought their families in great numbers to Yellow Ox Mountain for refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring districts, knowing they could rely on her, brought their families in great numbers to seek refuge on Yellow Ox Mountain.

sentences.zh: 有不能自給者，晏悉以家糧助之。

translations.literal: Those who could not support themselves—Yan aided them all with household grain.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not support themselves she aided with household grain.

sentences.zh: 於是聚眾日廣，復與倫、萬全共措置，析黃牛山為五砦，選少壯為義丁，有急則互相應援以為犄角，賊屢攻弗克。

translations.literal: Thereupon the gathered multitude grew daily; she again joined with Lun and Wanquan in arrangements, dividing Yellow Ox Mountain into five stockades, selecting the young and strong as righteous militia, and when urgent need arose mutually reinforcing one another in horn formation; the bandits attacked repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: The gathered multitude grew daily; joining with Lun and Wanquan, she divided Yellow Ox Mountain into five stockades, selected the young and strong as militia, and organized mutual reinforcement; the bandits attacked repeatedly without success.

sentences.zh: 所活老幼數萬人。

translations.literal: The old and young she preserved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: She preserved tens of thousands of old and young.

sentences.zh: 知南劍州陳韡遣人遺以金帛，晏悉散給其下；

translations.literal: Chen Wei, prefect of Nanjian, sent someone to present her with gold and silks; Yan distributed them all to her followers;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wei, prefect of Nanjian, sent gold and silks; Yan distributed them all to her followers;

sentences.zh: 又遺楮幣以勞五砦之義丁，且借補其子，名其砦曰萬安。

translations.literal: he also sent paper currency to reward the righteous militia of the five stockades and provisionally appointed her son, naming her stockade Ever-Peace.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent paper currency to reward the militia of the five stockades and provisionally appointed her son, naming her stockade Ever-Peace.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔特封晏為恭人，仍賜冠帔，其子特與補承信郎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict specially enfeoffed Yan as Lady, still granting cap and sash; her son was specially granted appointment as Gentleman for Trust.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict enfeoffed Yan as Lady with cap and sash, and specially appointed her son Gentleman for Trust.

sentences.zh: 王袤妻趙氏，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shi, wife of Wang Mao, was a native of Leping in Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shi, wife of Wang Mao, was from Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，袤監上高酒稅，金兵犯筠，袤棄官逃去，趙從之行。

translations.literal: During Jianyan, Mao supervised the wine tax at Shanggao; when Jin troops invaded Yun, Mao abandoned his post and fled, Zhao following on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyan Wang Mao supervised the wine tax at Shanggao; when Jin troops invaded Yun, he abandoned his post and fled, Zhao accompanying him.

sentences.zh: 遇金人，縛以去，係袤夫婦於劉氏門，而入剽掠劉室。

translations.literal: They encountered Jin troops, who bound them and took them away, tying Mao and his wife at the Liu family gate while entering to plunder the Liu household.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered Jin troops, who seized them, tied the couple at the Liu family gate, and entered to plunder the Liu household.

sentences.zh: 趙宛轉解縛，並解袤，謂袤曰：“君速去。

translations.literal: Zhao twisted free of her bonds and also freed Mao, saying to Mao: 'Husband, flee quickly.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao worked free of her bonds and freed Mao as well, telling him: 'Husband, flee quickly.'

sentences.zh: ”俄而金人出，問袤安往，趙他指以誤之。

translations.literal: Soon the Jin came out and asked where Mao had gone; Zhao pointed elsewhere to deceive them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jin emerged and asked where Mao had gone; Zhao pointed elsewhere to deceive them.

sentences.zh: 金人追之不得，怒趙欺己，殺之。

translations.literal: The Jin, unable to pursue him, grew angry that Zhao had deceived them and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to catch him, the Jin grew angry at her deception and killed her.

sentences.zh: 袤方伏叢薄間，望之悲痛，歸刻趙像以葬。

translations.literal: Mao was hiding in the thickets, watching in grief; he returned, carved Zhao's likeness, and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Mao hid in the thickets, watching in grief; he returned, carved her likeness, and buried it.

sentences.zh: 袤後仕至孝順監鎮。

translations.literal: Mao later served until he reached Supervisor of the Xiaoshun Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Mao later rose to Supervisor of the Xiaoshun Garrison.

sentences.zh: 塗端友妻陳氏，撫州臨川人。

translations.literal: Chen Shi, wife of Tu Duanyou, was a native of Linchuan in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi, wife of Tu Duanyou, was from Linchuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，盜起，被驅入黃山寺，賊逼之不從，以刃加其頸，叱曰：“汝輩鼠竊，命若蜉蝣，我良家子，義豈爾辱！

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose; she was driven into Huangshan Temple. The bandits pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck and shouted: 'You lot are rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing bandits rose and drove her into Huangshan Temple. They pressed her and she would not yield; they placed a blade to her neck and shouted: 'You are mere rat thieves—your lives are like mayflies; I am a respectable family's daughter—how could I suffer your disgrace!

sentences.zh: 縱殺我，官兵即至，爾其免乎？

translations.literal: Even if you kill me, government troops will soon arrive—will you not then escape?'
translations.idiomatic: Even if you kill me, government troops will soon arrive—will you not then escape?'

sentences.zh: ”賊知不可屈，乃幽之屋壁。

translations.literal: The bandits knew she could not be bent and imprisoned her within a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not be bent, the bandits imprisoned her within a wall.

sentences.zh: 居數日，族黨有得釋者，鹹齎金帛以贖其孥。

translations.literal: After several days, kinsmen who gained release all brought gold and silks to ransom their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, kinsmen who gained release brought gold and silks to ransom their families.

sentences.zh: 賊引端友妻令婦。

translations.literal: The bandits brought Duanyou's wife to meet the woman.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits brought Duanyou's wife to meet her.

sentences.zh: 曰：“吾聞貞女不出閨閣，今吾被驅至此，何面目登塗氏堂！

translations.literal: She said: 'I have heard that chaste women do not leave the inner quarters—now that I am driven here, what face have I to ascend the Tu clan's hall!
translations.idiomatic: She said: 'I have heard that chaste women do not leave the inner quarters—now that I am driven here, what face have I to enter the Tu clan's hall!

sentences.zh: ”復罵賊不絕，竟死之。

translations.literal: She cursed the bandits without cease and in the end was killed.
translations.idiomatic: She cursed the bandits without cease until they killed her.

sentences.zh: 詹氏女，蕪湖人。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Zhan clan was a native of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the Zhan clan was from Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，年十七，淮寇號“一窠蜂”倏破縣，女歎曰：“父子無俱生理，我計決矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, aged seventeen, when Huai bandits calling themselves 'One Nest of Bees' suddenly overran the county, the girl sighed: 'Father and son cannot both live—I have made my decision.'
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxing, when she was seventeen, Huai bandits calling themselves 'One Nest of Bees' suddenly overran the county. The girl sighed: 'Father and son cannot both survive—I have made my decision.'

sentences.zh: ”頃之賊至，欲殺其父兄，女趨而前拜曰：“妾雖窶陋，願執巾帚以事將軍，贖父兄命。

translations.literal: Soon the bandits arrived, wishing to kill her father and elder brother; the girl hurried forward and bowed, saying: 'Though I am poor and plain, I am willing to hold towel and comb to serve the general and ransom my father and brother's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bandits arrived, intending to kill her father and elder brother. The girl hurried forward and bowed: 'Though I am plain, I am willing to serve you as handmaid and ransom my father and brother's lives.

sentences.zh: 不然，父子並命，無益也。

translations.literal: Otherwise father and son will both die—to no purpose.'
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they will both die—to no purpose.'

sentences.zh: ”賊釋父兄縛，女麾手使亟去：“無顧我，我得侍將軍，何所憾哉。

translations.literal: The bandits released the father and brother's bonds; the girl waved her hand, urging them to flee quickly: 'Do not look back at me—now that I may serve the general, what regret have I?'
translations.idiomatic: The bandits released her father and brother. She waved them away: 'Flee quickly—do not look back. Now that I may serve you, what regret have I?'

sentences.zh: ”遂隨賊。

translations.literal: She then followed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: She then followed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 行數里，過市東橋，躍身入水死。

translations.literal: After traveling several li they passed the market's east bridge; she leaped into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: After traveling several li they passed the east bridge of the market; she leaped into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 賊相顧駭歎而去。

translations.literal: The bandits looked at one another in startled admiration and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits looked at one another in startled admiration and departed.

sentences.zh: 劉生妻歐陽氏，吉州安福人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Shi, wife of Liu Sheng, was a native of Anfu in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Shi, wife of Liu Sheng, was from Anfu in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 生居新樂鄉，以事出，惡少來欲侵淩之，歐陽不受辱而死。

translations.literal: Sheng lived in Xinle Township; when he went out on business, ruffians came wishing to molest her; Ouyang, refusing to suffer disgrace, died.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng lived in Xinle Township. When he went out on business, ruffians came to molest her; Ouyang refused to suffer disgrace and died.

sentences.zh: 邑人劉寬作詩以吊之，時紹興十年也。

translations.literal: Liu Kuan of the district composed a poem to mourn her—in the tenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuan of the district composed a poem to mourn her, in the tenth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 同縣有朱雲孫妻劉氏，姑病，雲孫刲股肉作糜以進而愈。

translations.literal: In the same county, Liu Shi, wife of Zhu Yunsun, when her mother-in-law fell ill, Yunsun cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel and presented it; she recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county, Liu Shi, wife of Zhu Yunsun, when her mother-in-law fell ill, Yunsun cut flesh from his thigh to make gruel for her and she recovered.

sentences.zh: 姑復病，劉亦刲股以進，又愈。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law fell ill again, Liu also cut flesh and presented it, and she recovered again.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill again, Liu also cut flesh from her thigh and presented it, and she recovered again.

sentences.zh: 尚書謝諤為賦《孝婦詩》。

translations.literal: Minister Xie E composed the Poem on the Filial Wife for them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xie E composed the Poem on the Filial Wife for them.

sentences.zh: 謝泌妻侯氏，南豐人。

translations.literal: Hou Shi, wife of Xie Bi, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shi, wife of Xie Bi, was from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 始笄，家貧，事姑孝謹。

translations.literal: When she first pinned up her hair, the family was poor; she served her mother-in-law with filial care and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age the family was poor; she served her mother-in-law with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 盜起，焚裏舍殺人，遠近逃避。

translations.literal: Bandits rose, burning neighborhood houses and killing people; near and far fled in escape.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose, burning houses and killing people; neighbors fled in all directions.

sentences.zh: 姑疾篤不能去，侯號泣姑側。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law was gravely ill and could not leave; Hou wailed and wept at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was gravely ill and could not flee; Hou wept at her side.

sentences.zh: 盜逼之，侯曰：“寧死不從。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed her; Hou said: 'Better die than submit.'
translations.idiomatic: The bandits pressed her; Hou said: 'I would rather die than submit.'

sentences.zh: ”盜刃之，仆溝中。

translations.literal: The bandits bladed her and she collapsed in the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits stabbed her and she fell into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 賊退，漸蘇，見一篋在側，發之皆金珠，族婦以為己物，侯悉歸之，婦分其一以謝，侯辭曰：“非我有，不願也。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated she gradually revived and saw a box beside her; opening it, it was all gold and pearls. A clanswoman took it for her own; Hou returned it all, and when the woman offered her a share in thanks, Hou declined: 'It is not mine—I do not wish it.'
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits retreated she gradually revived and found a box of gold and pearls beside her. A clanswoman claimed it as her own; Hou returned it all. When the woman offered her a share in thanks, Hou declined: 'It is not mine—I do not want it.'

sentences.zh: ”後夫與姑俱亡，子幼，父母欲更嫁之，侯曰：“兒以賤婦人，得歸隱居賢者之門已幸矣，忍去而使謝氏無後乎？

translations.literal: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to marry her off again. Hou said: 'My son, through a lowly woman's body, was fortunate to enter the gate of a reclusive worthy—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Later her husband and mother-in-law both died, leaving a young son; her parents wished to remarry her. Hou said: 'Through a lowly woman's body my son was fortunate to enter a worthy household—how could I leave and leave the Xie clan without posterity?

sentences.zh: 寧貧以養其子，雖餓死亦命也。

translations.literal: Better remain poor and rear my son—even if I starve to death, that is fate.'
translations.idiomatic: I would rather remain poor and rear my son—even if I starve, that is my fate.'

sentences.zh: 同縣有樂氏女，父以鬻果為業。

translations.literal: In the same county was the daughter of the Yue clan; her father made a living selling fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county was the daughter of the Yue clan; her father sold fruit for a living.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年，盜入境，其父買舟挈家走建昌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding bandits entered the district; her father bought a boat and took the family fleeing to Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoding bandits entered the district; her father bought a boat and took the family fleeing to Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 盜掠其舟，將逼二女，俱不從，一赴水死，一見殺。

translations.literal: Bandits seized their boat and were about to force the two daughters; both refused—one threw herself into the water and died, the other was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits seized their boat and tried to force the two daughters; both refused—one drowned herself, the other was killed.

sentences.zh: 謝枋得妻李氏，饒州安仁人也。

translations.literal: Li Shi, wife of Xie Fangde, was a native of Anren in Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, wife of Xie Fangde, was from Anren in Raozhou.
