sentences.zh: 色美而慧，通女訓諸書。

translations.literal: Beautiful and intelligent, she mastered the teachings for women and various books.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful and intelligent, she mastered women's teachings and various books.

sentences.zh: 嫁枋得，事舅姑、奉祭、待賓皆有禮。

translations.literal: Married to Fangde, in serving parents-in-law, conducting sacrifices, and receiving guests she observed all propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Married to Fangde, she observed all propriety in serving her parents-in-law, conducting sacrifices, and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 枋得起兵守安仁，兵敗逃入閩中。

translations.literal: Fangde raised troops to defend Anren; his army was defeated and he fled into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde raised troops to defend Anren; defeated, he fled into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 武萬戶以枋得豪傑，恐其扇變，購捕之，根及其家人。

translations.literal: Commander Wu of the military household, judging Fangde a heroic figure and fearing he might incite rebellion, offered a reward for his capture and rooted out his entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wu, judging Fangde a heroic figure and fearing he might incite rebellion, offered a reward for his capture and hunted down his entire family.

sentences.zh: 李氏攜二子匿貴溪山荊棘中，采草木而食。

translations.literal: Li Shi took her two sons and hid in the brambles of Guixi Mountain, gathering plants for food.
translations.idiomatic: Li took her two sons and hid in the brambles of Guixi Mountain, gathering wild plants for food.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年冬，信兵蹤跡至山中，令曰：“苟不獲李氏，屠而墟！

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Xin troops tracked them to the mountain; the order ran: 'If Li is not captured, slaughter all and leave the place a ruin!
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Xin troops tracked them to the mountain with the order: 'If Li is not captured, slaughter everyone and leave the place a ruin!

sentences.zh: ”李聞之，曰：“豈可以我故累人，吾出，事塞矣。

translations.literal: Li, hearing this, said: 'How can I bring disaster upon others because of myself—if I come out, the matter will be settled.'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Li said: 'How can I bring disaster on others because of me—if I surrender, the matter will end.'

sentences.zh: ”遂就俘。

translations.literal: She then gave herself up as captive.
translations.idiomatic: She then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙囚建康。

translations.literal: The next year the prisoners were moved to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the prisoners were moved to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 或指李言曰：“明當沒入矣。

translations.literal: Someone pointed at Li and said: 'Tomorrow she will be confiscated.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone pointed at Li and said: 'Tomorrow she will be confiscated.'

sentences.zh: ”李聞之，撫二子，淒然而泣。

translations.literal: Li, hearing this, embraced her two sons and wept mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Li embraced her two sons and wept.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：“雖沒入，將不失為官人妻，何泣也？

translations.literal: Those beside her said: 'Though confiscated, you will still become an official's wife—why weep?'
translations.idiomatic: Those beside her said: 'Even if confiscated, you will still become an official's wife—why weep?'

sentences.zh: ”李曰：“吾豈可嫁二夫耶！

translations.literal: Li said: 'How could I marry a second husband!'
translations.idiomatic: Li said: 'How could I marry a second husband!'

sentences.zh: ”顧謂二子曰：“若幸生還，善事吾姑，吾不得終養矣。

translations.literal: She turned to her two sons and said: 'If by fortune you survive, serve my mother-in-law well—I can no longer care for her to the end.'
translations.idiomatic: She told her sons: 'If you survive, serve your grandmother well—I can no longer care for her.'

sentences.zh: ”是夕，解裙帶自經獄中死。

translations.literal: That evening she removed her skirt sash and hanged herself in the prison.
translations.idiomatic: That evening she removed her skirt sash and hanged herself in prison.

sentences.zh: 枋得母桂氏尤賢達，自枋得逋播，婦與孫幽遠方，處之泰然，無一怨語。

translations.literal: Fangde's mother, the Lady Gui, was especially worthy and discerning; from the time Fangde became a fugitive, daughter-in-law and grandsons dwelt far away, yet she bore it calmly without a word of complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Fangde's mother, Lady Gui, was especially worthy; from the time he became a fugitive, his wife and grandsons dwelt far away, yet she bore it calmly without complaint.

sentences.zh: 人問之，曰：“義所當然也。

translations.literal: When people asked her, she said: 'It is what righteousness demands.'
translations.idiomatic: When people asked her, she said: 'It is what righteousness demands.'

sentences.zh: ”人稱為賢母雲。

translations.literal: People called her the Worthy Mother.
translations.idiomatic: People called her the Worthy Mother.

sentences.zh: 王貞婦，夫家臨海人也。

translations.literal: The chaste wife Wang—her husband's family were natives of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: The chaste widow Wang—her husband's family were natives of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 德祐二年冬，大元兵入浙東，婦與其舅、姑、夫皆被執。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Deyou, Great Yuan troops entered eastern Zhe; the woman, together with her father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband, were all seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Deyou, Yuan troops entered eastern Zhe; she, her father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband were all seized.

sentences.zh: 既而舅、姑與夫皆死，主將見婦皙美，欲內之，婦號慟欲自殺，為奪挽不得死。

translations.literal: Later her father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband all died; the commander, seeing the woman fair and beautiful, wished to take her within. She wailed and wished to kill herself, but they seized and restrained her so she could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Later her in-laws and husband all died; the commander, seeing her fair, wished to take her. She wailed and tried to kill herself, but they restrained her.

sentences.zh: 夜令俘囚婦人雜守之。

translations.literal: At night he ordered captive women to guard her in a mixed company.
translations.idiomatic: At night he ordered captive women to guard her.

sentences.zh: 婦乃陽謂主將曰：“若以吾為妻妾者，欲令終身善事主君也。

translations.literal: The woman then feigned to the commander: 'If you take me as wife or concubine, you wish me to serve the lord faithfully all my life.
translations.idiomatic: She then feigned to the commander: 'If you take me as wife or concubine, you wish me to serve you faithfully for life.

sentences.zh: 吾舅、姑與夫死，而我不為之衰，是不天也。

translations.literal: My father-in-law, mother-in-law, and husband are dead, yet I do not mourn for them—that would be to defy Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: My in-laws and husband are dead, yet I do not mourn them—that would defy Heaven.

sentences.zh: 不天之人，若將焉用之！

translations.literal: A person who defies Heaven—of what use would I be to you!'
translations.idiomatic: A person who defies Heaven—of what use would I be to you!

sentences.zh: 願請為服期，即惟命。

translations.literal: I beg to be allowed a mourning period, and then I am at your command.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me a mourning period, and then I am at your command.

sentences.zh: 苟不聽我，我終死耳，不能為若妻也。

translations.literal: If you will not heed me, I shall die in the end and cannot be your wife.'
translations.idiomatic: If you will not heed me, I shall die and cannot be your wife.'

sentences.zh: ”主將恐其誠死，許之，然防守益嚴。

translations.literal: The commander, fearing she would truly die, consented, yet the guard grew stricter still.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing she would truly die, the commander consented, yet tightened the guard.

sentences.zh: 明年春，師還，挈行至嵊青楓嶺，下臨絕壑。

translations.literal: The next spring the army returned, taking her as they marched to Qingfeng Ridge in Sheng, which overlooked a sheer ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring the army returned, marching her to Qingfeng Ridge in Sheng, overlooking a sheer ravine.

sentences.zh: 婦待守者少懈，齧指出血，書字山石上，南望慟哭，自投崖下而死。

translations.literal: When the guards slackened slightly, the woman bit her finger until blood flowed, wrote characters on the mountain stone, gazed southward and wailed, and threw herself from the cliff to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the guards slackened, she bit her finger until blood flowed, wrote on the cliff stone, gazed south and wailed, and threw herself from the cliff.

sentences.zh: 後其血皆漬入石間，盡化為石。

translations.literal: Later her blood all seeped into the stone and wholly turned to stone.
translations.idiomatic: Later her blood seeped into the stone and turned wholly to stone.

sentences.zh: 天且陰雨，即墳起如始書時。

translations.literal: When heaven was about to darken with rain, the writing on the tomb rose as when first inscribed.
translations.idiomatic: When rain was about to fall, the writing on her tomb appeared as when first inscribed.

sentences.zh: 至治中，朝廷旌之曰“貞婦”，郡守立石祠嶺上，易名曰清風嶺。

translations.literal: During the Zhizhi era the court commended her as 'Chaste Wife'; the prefect erected a stone shrine on the ridge and renamed it Clear Wind Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizhi era the court commended her as 'Chaste Wife'; the prefect erected a stone shrine on the ridge and renamed it Clear Wind Ridge.

sentences.zh: 趙淮妾，長沙人也，逸其姓名。

translations.literal: The concubine of Zhao Huai was a native of Changsha; her personal name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine of Zhao Huai was from Changsha; her personal name is lost.

sentences.zh: 德祐中，從淮戍銀樹埧。

translations.literal: During Deyou she followed the Huai garrison at Yingshu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: During Deyou she followed the Huai garrison at Yingshu Ford.

sentences.zh: 淮兵敗，俱執至瓜州。

translations.literal: The Huai army was defeated; all were seized and taken to Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai army was defeated; all were seized and taken to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 元帥阿術使淮招李庭芝，淮陽諾，至揚城下，乃大呼曰：“李庭芝，男子死耳，毋降也。

translations.literal: Marshal A Shu had Huai summon Li Tingzhi; Huai pretended assent and, reaching below Yang City, then shouted loudly: 'Li Tingzhi—a man should simply die; do not surrender!'
translations.idiomatic: Marshal A Shu had Huai summon Li Tingzhi. Huai feigned agreement and, reaching Yang City, shouted: 'Li Tingzhi—a man should die rather than surrender!'

sentences.zh: ”元帥怒，殺之，棄其屍江濱。

translations.literal: The marshal grew angry and killed him, casting his corpse on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the marshal killed him and cast his body on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 妾俘一軍校帳中，乃解衣中金遺其左右，且告之曰：“妾夙事趙運使，今其死不葬，妾誠不能忘情。

translations.literal: The concubine was captive in a military officer's tent; she removed gold from her garments and gave it to his attendants, also telling them: 'I long served Commissioner Zhao; now that he dies unburied, I truly cannot forget my feelings.'
translations.idiomatic: Held captive in a military officer's tent, she removed gold from her garments and gave it to his attendants, saying: 'I long served Commissioner Zhao; now that he lies unburied, I cannot forget him.'

sentences.zh: 願因公言使掩埋之，當終身事相公無憾矣。

translations.literal: I beg that through your lordship's words he may be buried; then I may serve the lord for life without regret.'
translations.idiomatic: Please ask your lord to have him buried; then I will serve you for life without regret.'

sentences.zh: ”軍校憐其言，使數兵輿如江上。

translations.literal: The military officer pitied her words and sent several soldiers with sedan chairs to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying her words, the officer sent soldiers with a litter to the river.

sentences.zh: 妾聚薪焚淮骨置瓦缶中，自抱持，操小舟至急流，仰天慟哭，躍水而死。

translations.literal: The concubine gathered firewood, burned Huai's bones, placed them in an earthen jar, embraced it herself, poled a small boat to the rapids, looked up to heaven and wailed bitterly, and leaped into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: She gathered firewood, burned Huai's bones, placed them in a jar, embraced it, poled a small boat to the rapids, wailed to heaven, and leaped into the water.

sentences.zh: 譚氏婦趙，吉州永新人。

translations.literal: Zhao, wife of the Tan clanswoman, was a native of Yongxin in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, wife of the Tan clanswoman, was from Yongxin in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，江南既內附，永新復嬰城自守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, after the south of the Yangtze had submitted, Yongxin again closed its walls and held out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, after the south had submitted, Yongxin again held its walls and resisted.

sentences.zh: 天兵破城，趙氏抱嬰兒隨其舅、姑同匿邑校中，為悍卒所獲，殺其舅、姑，執趙欲汙之，不可，臨之以刃曰：“從我則生，不從則死。

translations.literal: Heaven's troops broke the city; Zhao Shi, holding her infant, hid with her uncle and mother-in-law in the district schoolhouse, was seized by brutal soldiers who killed her uncle and mother-in-law, seized Zhao wishing to defile her—she would not yield—and they pressed her with blades, saying: 'Follow me and live; refuse and die.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan troops took the city. Zhao, holding her infant, hid with her uncle and mother-in-law in the district school but was seized by brutal soldiers who killed her uncle and mother-in-law. They seized Zhao and tried to violate her; she refused. They threatened her with blades: 'Follow me and live; refuse and die.'

sentences.zh: ”趙罵曰：“吾舅死於汝，吾姑又死於汝，吾與其不義而生，寧從吾舅、姑以死耳。

translations.literal: Zhao cursed: 'My uncle died at your hands, my mother-in-law also died at your hands—I would rather die with my uncle and mother-in-law than live in what is unrighteous.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cursed: 'My uncle died by your hand, my mother-in-law by your hand—I would rather die with them than live in unrighteousness.'

sentences.zh: ”遂與嬰兒同遇害。

translations.literal: She then perished together with her infant.
translations.idiomatic: She and her infant were killed together.

sentences.zh: 血漬於禮殿兩楹之間，入磚為婦人與嬰兒狀，久而宛然如新。

translations.literal: Blood stained between the two pillars of the ritual hall; entering the brick it formed the shapes of a woman and infant, and for long remained as fresh as new.
translations.idiomatic: Blood stained the two pillars of the ritual hall; soaking into the brick it formed the shapes of a woman and infant, remaining fresh for a long time.

sentences.zh: 或訝之，磨以沙石不滅，又段以熾炭，其狀益顯。

translations.literal: When people were startled, grinding with sand and stone did not efface it; heating with blazing charcoal, the image grew even clearer.
translations.idiomatic: When people were startled, grinding with sand and stone could not efface it; heating with blazing charcoal made the image even clearer.

sentences.zh: 吳中孚妻，隆興之進賢人，少寡。

translations.literal: The wife of Wu Zhongfu was a native of Jinxian in Longxing; she became a widow while young.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Wu Zhongfu was from Jinxian in Longxing and became a widow while young.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，兵亂，攜孤女自沈於縣之染步，曰：“義不辱吾夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding, amid military turmoil, she took her orphaned daughter and drowned herself at Ranbu in the county, saying: 'I choose righteousness—I will not disgrace my husband.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingding, amid military turmoil, she took her orphaned daughter and drowned herself at Ranbu, saying: 'I will not disgrace my husband.'

sentences.zh: 呂仲洙女，名良子，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: The daughter of Lu Zhongzhu, named Liangzi, was a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Lu Zhongzhu, named Liangzi, was from Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父得疾瀕殆，女焚香祝天，請以身代，刲股為粥以進。

translations.literal: Her father fell gravely ill near death; the girl burned incense and prayed to Heaven, asking to substitute her own body, cut flesh from her thigh to make gruel and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Her father fell gravely ill; the girl burned incense and prayed to Heaven to substitute her own body, cut flesh from her thigh to make gruel, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 時夜中，群鵲繞屋飛噪，仰視空中，大星燁煜如月者三。

translations.literal: In the depth of night a flock of magpies circled the house flying and crying; looking up into the sky, three great stars blazed bright as the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the night magpies circled the house crying; looking up, three great stars blazed bright as the moon.

sentences.zh: 越翼日，父瘳。

translations.literal: The next day her father recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day her father recovered.

sentences.zh: 女弟細良亦相從拜禱，良子卻之，細良恚曰：“豈姊能之，兒不能耶！

translations.literal: Her younger sister Xiliang also wished to join in worship and prayer; Liangzi refused her, and Xiliang said angrily: 'Can elder sister do it but I cannot!'
translations.idiomatic: Her younger sister Xiliang also wished to join in prayer; Liangzi refused, and Xiliang said angrily: 'If my sister can do it, why cannot I!'

sentences.zh: ”守真德秀嘉之，表其居曰“懿孝”。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhen Dexiu praised them and marked their dwelling 'Exemplary Filial Piety.'
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhen Dexiu praised them and marked their dwelling 'Exemplary Filial Piety.'

sentences.zh: 林老女，永春人，及笄未婚。

translations.literal: The old woman of the Lin family was a native of Yongchun; she came of age unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: Old woman Lin was from Yongchun and came of age unmarried.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年夏，寇犯邑，入山避之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Shaoding bandits invaded the district; she entered the mountains to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Shaoding bandits invaded the district; she fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 猝遇寇，欲汙之，不從。

translations.literal: She suddenly encountered bandits who wished to defile her; she would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: She suddenly encountered bandits who tried to violate her; she refused.

sentences.zh: 度不得脫，紿曰：“有金帛埋於家，盍同取之？

translations.literal: Judging she could not escape, she deceived them: 'There is gold and silk buried at home—why not go together to fetch it?'
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not escape, she deceived them: 'I have gold and silk buried at home—come fetch it with me.'

sentences.zh: ”甫入門，大呼曰：“吾寧死於家，決不辱吾身。

translations.literal: Just inside the gate she shouted loudly: 'I would rather die at home than disgrace my body.'
translations.idiomatic: Just inside the gate she shouted: 'I would rather die at home than disgrace myself.'

sentences.zh: ”賊怒殺之，越三日麵如生。

translations.literal: The bandits angrily killed her; after three days her face was as in life.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed her in anger; three days later her face was as in life.

sentences.zh: 童八娜，鄞之通遠鄉建奧人。

translations.literal: Tong Bana was a native of Jian'ao in Tongyuan Township, Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Bana was from Jian'ao in Tongyuan Township, Yin.

sentences.zh: 虎銜其大母，女手拽虎尾，祈以身代。

translations.literal: A tiger seized her paternal grandmother; the girl grasped the tiger's tail with her hand and prayed to substitute her own body.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger seized her grandmother; the girl grasped its tail and begged to take her grandmother's place.

sentences.zh: 虎為釋其大母，銜女以去。

translations.literal: The tiger released her grandmother and carried off the girl.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger released her grandmother and carried off the girl.

sentences.zh: 始，林栗侍親官其地，嚐目睹之。

translations.literal: At first Lin Li, attending his parents in office there, once witnessed it with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Li, then attending his parents in office there, once witnessed it himself.

sentences.zh: 已而為守，以聞於朝，祠祀之。

translations.literal: Later he became prefect, reported it to the court, and she received temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as prefect, he reported it to the court and she received temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 韓氏女，字希孟，巴陵人，或曰丞相琦之裔。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Han clan, styled Ximeng, was a native of Baling—or said to be a descendant of Chancellor Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the Han clan, styled Ximeng, was from Baling—some say a descendant of Chancellor Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 少明慧，知讀書。

translations.literal: Young, bright and clever, she knew how to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Young, bright and clever, she could read books.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，大元兵至嶽陽，女年十有八，為卒所掠，將挾以獻其主將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing the Great Yuan army reached Yueyang; the girl was eighteen and was seized by soldiers, who wished to take her to present to their commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiqing the Yuan army reached Yueyang; the girl was eighteen when soldiers seized her to present to their commander.

sentences.zh: 女知必不免，竟赴水死。

translations.literal: The girl knew she could not escape and at last threw herself into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she could not escape, she threw herself into the water.

sentences.zh: 越三日得其屍，於練裙帶有詩曰：“我質本瑚璉，宗廟供頻蘩。

translations.literal: Three days later they recovered her corpse; on her silk skirt band was a poem: 'My substance was originally ritual jade, for the ancestral temple offered fragrant herbs again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later they recovered her body; on her silk skirt was a poem: 'My substance was ritual jade, meant for the ancestral temple's offerings.

sentences.zh: 一朝嬰禍難，失身戎馬間。

translations.literal: One morning I met calamity and hardship, losing my person among war-horses.
translations.idiomatic: One morning calamity struck, and I was lost among war-horses.

sentences.zh: 寧當血刃死，不作衽席完。

translations.literal: Better to die beneath the bloody blade than be made whole upon the marriage bed.
translations.idiomatic: Better to die by the blade than be made whole on the marriage bed.

sentences.zh: 漢上有王猛，江南無謝安。

translations.literal: On the Han there is Wang Meng; in the south of the Yangtze there is no Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: On the Han there is a Wang Meng; in Jiangnan there is no Xie An.

sentences.zh: 長號赴洪流，激烈摧心肝。

translations.literal: With long wailing I rush to the mighty torrent, fiercely shattering heart and liver.'
translations.idiomatic: With long wailing I rush to the mighty torrent, shattering heart and liver.'

sentences.zh: 王氏婦梁，臨川人。

translations.literal: Liang, wife of the Wang clanswoman, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, wife of the Wang clanswoman, was from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 歸夫家才數月，會大元兵至，一夕，與夫約曰：“吾遇兵必死，義不受汙辱。

translations.literal: She had returned to her husband's family only a few months when the Great Yuan army arrived; one evening she agreed with her husband: 'If I meet soldiers I must die—I will not suffer disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: She had been married only a few months when the Yuan army arrived. One evening she told her husband: 'If soldiers come I must die—I will not suffer disgrace.'

sentences.zh: 若後娶，當告我。

translations.literal: If you marry again afterward, you must tell me.'
translations.idiomatic: If you remarry, you must tell me.'

sentences.zh: ”頃之，夫婦被掠。

translations.literal: Soon husband and wife were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were seized together.

sentences.zh: 有軍千戶強使從己，婦紿曰：“夫在，伉儷之情有所不忍，乞歸之而後可。

translations.literal: A military chiliarch forcibly wished her to follow him; the woman deceived him: 'My husband is present—the feeling between husband and wife is hard to bear; let me return to him and then I may comply.'
translations.idiomatic: A chiliarch tried to take her; she deceived him: 'My husband is here—I cannot bear to leave him; let me return to him first.'

sentences.zh: ”千戶以所得金帛與其夫而歸之，並與一矢，以卻後兵。

translations.literal: The chiliarch gave the gold and silks he had obtained to her husband and sent her back, also giving an arrow to repel soldiers who came after.
translations.idiomatic: The chiliarch gave the gold and silks to her husband and sent her back, also giving an arrow to ward off pursuers.

sentences.zh: 約行十餘里，千戶即之，婦拒且罵曰：“斫頭奴！

translations.literal: They had gone about ten-odd li when the chiliarch overtook them; the woman resisted and cursed: 'Head-chopping slave!'
translations.idiomatic: After about ten li the chiliarch caught up; she resisted and cursed: 'Head-chopping slave!'

sentences.zh: 吾與夫誓，天地鬼神寔臨之，此身寧死不可得也。

translations.literal: I swore with my husband—Heaven, earth, ghosts, and spirits truly witnessed; this body would rather die than be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: I swore with my husband before Heaven and earth—this body would rather die than yield.'

sentences.zh: ”因奮搏之，乃被殺。

translations.literal: She then struggled fiercely and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: She struggled fiercely and was killed.

sentences.zh: 有同掠脫歸者道其事。

translations.literal: Someone seized together with them who escaped and returned reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow captive who escaped reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 越數年，夫以無嗣謀更娶，議輒不諧，因告其故妻，夜夢妻曰：“我死後生某氏家，今十歲矣。

translations.literal: Several years later, because he had no heir the husband planned to remarry; discussions repeatedly failed to agree, so he told his former wife's story; that night he dreamed his wife said: 'After my death I was born into such-and-such a clan's household; I am now ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, childless, he planned to remarry but could not agree on a match, so he told his wife's story. That night he dreamed she said: 'After my death I was reborn in a certain clan; I am now ten.'

sentences.zh: 後七年，當復為君婦。

translations.literal: In seven more years I shall again become your wife.'
translations.idiomatic: In seven more years I shall again be your wife.'

sentences.zh: ”明日遣人聘之，一言而合。

translations.literal: The next day he sent someone to betroth her; with one word all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent a betrothal party; with one word all was settled.

sentences.zh: 詢其生，與婦死年月同雲。

translations.literal: Inquiring into her birth, it matched the year and month of the woman's death.
translations.idiomatic: Her birth year and month matched the wife's death.

sentences.zh: 劉仝子妻林氏，福州福清人。

translations.literal: Lin Shi, wife of Liu Tongzi, was a native of Fuqing in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shi, wife of Liu Tongzi, was from Fuqing in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父公遇，知名士。

translations.literal: Her father Gongyu was a renowned scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Gongyu was a renowned scholar.

sentences.zh: 仝子為福建招撫使起義兵，事見《林同傳》。

translations.literal: Tongzi, as Fujian Pacification Commissioner, raised righteous troops—the affair is treated in the Biographies of Lin Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzi, as Fujian Pacification Commissioner, raised loyal troops—see the Biography of Lin Tong.

sentences.zh: 仝子亡命自經死，有司執其妻具反狀，林叱曰：“林、劉二族，世為宋臣，欲以忠義報國，事不成，天也，何為反乎！

translations.literal: Tongzi, a fugitive, hanged himself; the authorities seized his wife to compile evidence of rebellion. Lin rebuked them: 'The Lin and Liu clans for generations have been Song subjects, wishing to repay the state with loyalty and righteousness; the affair did not succeed—that is Heaven's will; why call it rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Tongzi hanged himself as a fugitive; authorities seized his wife to compile evidence of rebellion. Lin rebuked them: 'The Lin and Liu clans have been Song subjects for generations, wishing to serve with loyalty; we failed—that is Heaven's will; why call it rebellion!

sentences.zh: 汝知去歲有以血書壁而死者乎？

translations.literal: Do you know who last year wrote in blood on the wall and died?'
translations.idiomatic: Do you know who last year wrote in blood on the wall and died?'

sentences.zh: 是吾兄也。

translations.literal: That was my elder brother.'
translations.idiomatic: That was my elder brother.'

sentences.zh: 吾與兄，忠義之心則一也，死且求治汝於地下，可生為汝等淩辱耶！

translations.literal: My brother and I—our hearts of loyalty and righteousness are one; dead, I shall still seek justice for you in the underworld—how could I live and suffer your abuse!'
translations.idiomatic: My brother and I share one heart of loyalty; dead, I shall still seek justice from you underground—how could I live to suffer your abuse!'

sentences.zh: ”遂遇害。

translations.literal: She was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: She was then killed.

sentences.zh: 毛惜惜者，高郵妓女也。

translations.literal: Mao Xixi was a courtesan of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xixi was a courtesan of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 端平二年，別將榮全率眾據城以畔，製置使遣人以武翼郎招之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duanping, Vice General Rong Quan led a crowd in holding the city in rebellion; the Commissioner dispatched someone with the title Martial Wing Gentleman to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duanping Vice General Rong Quan rebelled and held the city; the Commissioner sent a Martial Wing Gentleman to summon him.

sentences.zh: 全偽降，欲殺使者，方與同黨王安等宴飲，惜惜恥於供給，安斥責之，惜惜曰：“初謂太尉降，為太尉更生賀。

translations.literal: Quan feigned surrender, wishing to kill the envoy; just as he was feasting with his accomplice Wang An and others, Xixi was shamed at serving them; An scolded her, and Xixi said: 'At first I thought the Grand Marshal had surrendered and came to congratulate him on his rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: Quan feigned surrender, planning to kill the envoy. As he feasted with Wang An and others, Xixi was shamed at serving them. An scolded her; she said: 'At first I thought the Grand Marshal had surrendered and came to congratulate his rebirth.

sentences.zh: 今乃閉門不納使者，縱酒不法，乃畔逆耳。

translations.literal: Now you close the gates and will not admit the envoy, indulging in wine against the law—you are truly rebels.'
translations.idiomatic: Now you shut the gates against the envoy and drink lawlessly—you are rebels.'

sentences.zh: 妾雖賤妓，不能事畔臣。

translations.literal: Though I am a lowly courtesan, I cannot serve rebel subjects.'
translations.idiomatic: Though I am a lowly courtesan, I cannot serve rebels.'

sentences.zh: ”全怒，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Quan grew angry and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Quan killed her.

sentences.zh: 越三日，李虎破關，禽全斬之，並其妻子及王安以下預畔者百有餘人悉傅以法。

translations.literal: Three days later Li Hu broke through the pass, captured Quan and beheaded him, together with his wife and children and Wang An and all who had joined the rebellion—more than a hundred in all—executing them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Li Hu broke the pass, captured Quan and beheaded him, together with his wife, children, Wang An, and more than a hundred rebels—all executed by law.
